Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team liked the idea of prefix caching and the dedicated pool options. Before we can route the order form to procurement, Legal asked for tighter language and concrete timelines around deletion and custody handback. Specifically: 1) we need a maximum timeline for final data wipe after contract termination for PHI-derived artifacts, 2) whether backups/snapshots are considered part of the same deletion window, and 3) whether there is support for a short ephemeral (14-day) nearline window for debug logs only.

I've attached a short worksheet with the baseline requirements from our Compliance team (MedBridge_SLA_Questions.xlsx). Can your order form call out these bespoke windows? If so, what does the signature-friendly clause look like?

Thanks — Emily

Emily —

Appreciate the worksheet, and yes we can capture bespoke retention and deletion language on the Order Form. I've looped in Rishi (AE) and Priyom (Solutions) so we can get precise timelines and the exact clause text for procurement. High-level response:

- We can provide a 14-day ephemeral nearline tier for debug/logs that are explicitly scoped.
- For customer-generated content (including PHI-derived artifacts), we offer configurable residency and a guaranteed final-deletion window after termination — typically quoted as a maximum of N days in the Order Form; we can propose a 90-day standard or accelerate to 30 days for an addendum.
- Backups/snapshots are treated separately in policy; we can either include them in the same deletion window or require a certified purge attestation (per your preference).

Priyom will follow up with the suggested wording and an internal timeline diagram. If that looks good, Rishi will draft the Order Form amendment and we can get Legal redlines.

Will attach a draft in a follow-up.

Best,
Soojin Lee

Soojin —

Thanks. A couple quick clarifications from Legal & Compliance after they skimmed the worksheet:

1) "Final-deletion window" — they want the maximum time from termination to irrevocable deletion spelled out, and a commitment on the notification cadence when deletion begins/completes.
2) "Backups" — Compliance prefers backups be included in the deletion window wherever possible; if not included, we need a certification process/error budget for delayed snapshot purges.
3) "Ephemeral logs" — Security asked that ephemeral logs be isolated and auditable; is the 14-day window implemented as an isolated bucket with a hard TTL?

If you could send the exact clause language and a quick technical note on how the ephemeral window is enforced (TTL vs manual purge), legal can review faster. Also please indicate any additional costs for accelerating deletion to 30 days for PHI-derived artifacts.

Regards,
Emily

Hi Emily —

Thanks for the follow-ups. Below is the concrete clause language we recommend for the Order Form plus the technical enforcement notes. I've kept the legal phrasing intentionally straightforward so procurement can paste into the amendment.

Recommended Order Form language (suggested insertion as Section 4.2 - Data Retention and Deletion):

"1) Retention classes and timelines. Customer data will be assigned to one of three retention classes as defined in this Order Form:
   a) Operational Content (includes customer prompts, model responses, and PHI-derived artifacts): final-deletion will commence upon contract termination and be completed within 90 calendar days, unless Customer elects the Accelerated Deletion Addendum below.
   b) Ephemeral Logs (debug/troubleshooting logs): retained in a logically isolated nearline bucket with a hard TTL of 14 calendar days from time of ingestion; data in this class will be automatically purged at TTL expiration.
   c) Backups and Snapshots: retained for no more than 180 calendar days post-termination unless Customer and Redwood agree to a different documented schedule. Backups are within scope of deletion for purposes of this clause unless an authorised restore is pending; otherwise Redwood will provide a certification of purge upon request.

2) Accelerated Deletion Addendum. Customer may purchase an Accelerated Deletion Addendum to reduce Operational Content final-deletion to 30 calendar days following termination; Redwood will provide a signed purge attestation upon completion for covered data classes.

3) Notification and attestation. Redwood will notify the Customer at the start of the deletion process and again upon completion by email to the contract owner on file. The Order Form will include a link to a downloadable purge attestation (PDF) containing record identifiers and timestamps.

4) Restoration holds. Customer-initiated restore holds must be requested in writing and may delay final-deletion for the requested duration. Each restore hold will be time-boxed and documented in Redwood's change log.
"

Technical enforcement notes (for Compliance):
- Ephemeral Logs: enforced via an isolated storage tier with bucket-level TTL; objects older than 14 days are expired automatically by the storage service (no manual step).
- Operational Content: primary deletion is performed programmatically from live stores; backups/snapshots require a certified purge job that removes incremental snapshots and records an attestation. Our automated purge jobs have a standard processing window (parallelized) which is accounted for in the 90-day and 30-day timelines.
- Backups: if Customer opts out of backup-inclusion, Redwood will provide a documented remediation runway and a monthly snapshot purge schedule; outstanding snapshots will be listed in the purge attestation.

Cost notes:
- Accelerated Deletion Addendum (90->30 days) is billable as a one-time Order Form fee; exact pricing depends on dataset size and residency (Priyom to coordinate with Rishi for a quote).

Next steps (proposed):
1) Emily: confirm whether backups must be included in the same deletion window or if MedBridge prefers a separate certification process.
2) Priyom: once confirmed, we'll produce a redline-ready Order Form amendment and a one-page timeline diagram (attached).
3) Rishi: prepare quote for Accelerated Deletion Addendum and add to HubSpot deal DB-8591.

Attachments: timeline-diagram.png (simple swimlane showing termination -> purge steps), SOC2-evidence-checklist.pdf (what we can provide for attestations).

Happy to hop on a short call if Legal wants to review wording live.
